ai.title: Ovarian Function and Pathology
ai.subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
ai.summary: The ovaries produce oocytes and hormones, regulate menstrual cycles, and are prone to infections, cysts, and malignancy in low‑resource settings. Clinical assessment focuses on pain, bleeding, and systemic signs.

sections.p: The ovaries are paired almond‑shaped organs in the pelvis that release eggs and secrete estrogen and progesterone. They are central to reproduction and menstrual regulation.

b: Follicular phase: estrogen rise, LH surge
sections.p: Ovarian function is governed by the hypothalamic‑pituitary‑gonadal axis. Dysregulation leads to amenorrhoea, infertility, or hormonal excess.

b: PID often presents with lower abdominal pain, fever, and purulent discharge
sections.p: In East Africa, common ovarian problems include pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), ovarian torsion, cystic disease, and ovarian cancer. HIV, TB, and schistosomiasis can complicate presentations.

sections.p: History and exam guide diagnosis. Look for acute onset pain, fever, adnexal tenderness, and signs of systemic infection. In torsion, pain is sudden, often with nausea, and the uterus may be displaced.

b: Use broad‑spectrum antibiotics covering N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis in PID
sections.p: Assuming normal CA‑125 rules out cancer; missing torsion due to low suspicion; over‑relying on ultrasound when quality is poor; treating PID with antibiotics alone without considering surgical source.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe abdominal pain with vomiting, fever >38.5°C, tachycardia, hypotension, or signs of shock
